The notation follows the [Deep Learning Book](https://www.deeplearningbook.org/contents/notation.html) [@goodfellow_deep_2016] where possible. Deviations and course-specific symbols are listed at the end of this page.

## Numbers and Arrays

| Syntax    | Description                |
|-----------|----------------------------|
| $a$    | A scalar (integer or real) |
| $\vect{a}$ | A vector                   |
| $\m{A}$  | A matrix                   |
| $\tensor{A}$ | A tensor                   |
| $\m{I}_n$ | Identity matrix with $n$ rows and $n$ columns |
| $\m{I}$ | Identity matrix with dimensionality implied by context |
| $\vect{0}$ | Vector of zeros with dimensionality implied by context |
| $\vect{e}^{(i)}$ | Standard basis vector $[0,\dots,0,1,0,\dots,0]$ with a 1 at position $i$ |
| $\text{diag}(\vect{a})$ | A square, diagonal matrix with diagonal entries given by $\vect{a}$ |
| $\rand{a}$ | A scalar random variable |
| $\vrand{a}$ | A vector-valued random variable |
| $\theta$ | Parameters of a model |


## Sets

| Syntax    | Description                |
|-----------|----------------------------|
| $\mathcal{A}$ | A set |
| $\mathbb{R}$ | The set of real numbers |
| $\mathbb{R}^{d}$, $\mathbb{R}^{m \times n}$ | The set of real vectors with $d$ entries, of real matrices with $m$ rows and $n$ columns |
| $\{0, 1, \dots, n\}$ | The set of all integers between $0$ and $n$ |
| $[a, b]$ | The real interval including $a$ and $b$ |
| $(a, b]$ | The real interval excluding $a$ but including $b$ |


## Indexing

| Syntax    | Description                |
|-----------|----------------------------|
| $a_i$ | Element $i$ of vector $\vect{a}$, with indexing starting at 1 |
| $A_{i,j}$ | Element $i, j$ of matrix $\m{A}$ |
| $\m{A}_{i,:}$ | Row $i$ of matrix $\m{A}$ |
| $\m{A}_{:,i}$ | Column $i$ of matrix $\m{A}$ |
| $\tensor{A}_{i,j,k}$ | Element $(i, j, k)$ of a 3-D tensor $\tensor{A}$ |
| $\m{W}^{(l)}$, $\vect{h}^{(l)}$ | Weights and activations of layer $l$ |


## Linear Algebra Operations

| Syntax    | Description                |
|-----------|----------------------------|
| $\m{A}^\top$ | Transpose of matrix $\m{A}$ |
| $\m{A} \odot \m{B}$ | Element-wise (Hadamard) product of $\m{A}$ and $\m{B}$ |
| $\det(\m{A})$ | Determinant of $\m{A}$ |
| $\operatorname{tr}(\m{A})$ | Trace of $\m{A}$ |


## Calculus

| Syntax    | Description                |
|-----------|----------------------------|
| $\frac{dy}{dx}$ | Derivative of $y$ with respect to $x$ |
| $\frac{\partial y}{\partial x}$ | Partial derivative of $y$ with respect to $x$ |
| $\nabla_{\vect{x}} y$ | Gradient of $y$ with respect to $\vect{x}$ |
| $\frac{\partial f}{\partial \vect{x}} \in \mathbb{R}^{m \times n}$ | Jacobian matrix of $f: \mathbb{R}^n \rightarrow \mathbb{R}^m$ |
| $\int f(\vect{x}) \, d\vect{x}$ | Definite integral over the entire domain of $\vect{x}$ |


## Probability and Information Theory

| Syntax    | Description                |
|-----------|----------------------------|
| $P(x)$ | A probability distribution over a discrete variable |
| $p(x)$ | A probability distribution over a continuous variable or over a variable whose type has not been specified |
| $p(\vect{x} \mid \vect{y})$ | Conditional distribution of $\vect{x}$ given $\vect{y}$ |
| $\vect{x} \sim p$ | $\vect{x}$ is sampled from (has distribution) $p$ |
| $\mathbb{E}_{\vect{x} \sim p} [ f(\vect{x}) ]$ | Expectation of $f(\vect{x})$ with respect to $p(\vect{x})$ |
| $D_{\mathrm{KL}}(P \,\Vert\, Q)$ | Kullback-Leibler divergence of $P$ and $Q$ |
| $\mathcal{N}(\vect{x}; \vect{\mu}, \m{\Sigma})$ | Gaussian distribution over $\vect{x}$ with mean $\vect{\mu}$ and covariance $\m{\Sigma}$ |
| $\mathcal{N}(x; \mu, \sigma^2)$ | Gaussian distribution over $x$ with mean $\mu$ and variance $\sigma^2$ |
| $\vect{z} \sim \mathcal{N}(\vect{0}, \m{I})$ | $\vect{z}$ is sampled from a standard Gaussian |


## Functions

| Syntax    | Description                |
|-----------|----------------------------|
| $f: \mathcal{A} \rightarrow \mathcal{B}$ | The function $f$ with domain $\mathcal{A}$ and range $\mathcal{B}$ |
| $f \circ g$ | Composition of the functions $f$ and $g$ |
| $f_\theta(\vect{x})$ | A function (model) of $\vect{x}$ with parameters $\theta$ |
| $\log x$ | The natural logarithm of $x$ |
| $\sigma(x)$ | Logistic sigmoid, $\frac{1}{1 + \exp(-x)}$ |
| $\mathrm{softmax}(\vect{z})$ | Softmax, $\mathrm{softmax}(\vect{z})_k = \frac{\exp(z_k)}{\sum_{j=1}^K \exp(z_j)}$ |
| $\mathrm{ReLU}(x)$ | Rectified linear unit, $\max(0, x)$ |
| $\lVert \vect{x} \rVert_p$ | $L^p$ norm of $\vect{x}$ |
| $\lVert \vect{x} \rVert$ | $L^2$ norm of $\vect{x}$ |
| $\floor{x}$ | $x$ rounded down to the nearest integer |
| $\arg\min_{\theta} f(\theta)$ | The value of $\theta$ that minimizes $f(\theta)$ |


## Datasets and Learning

| Syntax    | Description                |
|-----------|----------------------------|
| $N$ | Number of training examples |
| $d$ | Number of input features (dimensionality of $\vect{x}$) |
| $K$ | Number of classes |
| $\mathcal{D} = \{(\vect{x}^{(i)}, y^{(i)})\}_{i=1}^N$ | A training set |
| $\vect{x}^{(i)}$ | The $i$-th training example |
| $y^{(i)}$, $\vect{y}^{(i)}$ | The target (label or label vector) of the $i$-th training example |
| $\hat{y}$, $\hat{\vect{y}}$ | A model prediction |
| $\m{X} \in \mathbb{R}^{N \times d}$ | The design matrix, with example $\vect{x}^{(i)}$ in row $\m{X}_{i,:}$ |
| $p_{\text{data}}$ | The data-generating distribution |
| $L(\hat{y}, y)$ | Loss of a single example |
| $J(\theta)$ | Cost (objective): the loss averaged over the training set |
| $\theta^*$ | Optimal parameters, $\theta^* = \arg\min_{\theta} J(\theta)$ |


## Course-Specific Notation

The following symbols are not covered by the Deep Learning Book.

### Images and CNNs

| Syntax    | Description                |
|-----------|----------------------------|
| $C \times H \times W$ | Shape of an image or activation map: channels, height, width |
| $N \times C \times H \times W$ | Shape of a batch of $N$ images (NCHW, the format used by PyTorch) |
| $C_{in}$, $C_{out}$ | Number of input and output channels of a layer |
| $i$, $o$ | Spatial input and output size of a convolution |
| $k$, $s$, $p$, $d$ | Kernel size, stride, padding, dilation |
| $K * I$ | Convolution (implemented as cross-correlation) of input $I$ with kernel $K$ |
| $r_0$ | Receptive field size |

### Representation Learning

| Syntax    | Description                |
|-----------|----------------------------|
| $\vect{z} = f(\vect{x})$ | Representation (embedding) of $\vect{x}$ |
| $\mathrm{sim}(\vect{z}_i, \vect{z}_j)$ | Similarity of two representations, usually cosine similarity |
| $\tau$ | Temperature |

### Generative Models

| Syntax    | Description                |
|-----------|----------------------------|
| $p_\theta(\vect{x})$ | Model distribution with parameters $\theta$ |
| $\vect{z}$ | Latent variable / random input of a generative model |
| $\vect{c}$ | Condition (e.g. class label, text prompt) |
| $g$, $d$ | Generator, discriminator |
| $q_\psi(\vect{z} \mid \vect{x})$ | Encoder (approximate posterior) of a VAE |
| $\vect{x}_t$, $T$ | Sample at time step $t$, number of time steps (diffusion, flows) |
| $\vect{\epsilon}$ | Gaussian noise |
| $v_\theta(\vect{x}_t, t)$ | Velocity field (flow matching) |


## Deviations from the Deep Learning Book

- Models are written as $f_\theta(\vect{x})$ instead of $f(\vect{x}; \theta)$, as in most of the generative modelling literature.
- The number of training examples is $N$ (instead of $m$) and the number of input features is $d$ (instead of $n$).
- Sets are calligraphic ($\mathcal{D}$) instead of blackboard bold.
- Vectors and matrices are upright bold ($\vect{x}$, $\m{X}$) instead of bold italic.
- Pairs of examples in similarity and contrastive formulas are written as $\vect{z}_i, \vect{z}_j$ instead of $\vect{z}^{(i)}, \vect{z}^{(j)}$, following the original papers.
- Named objectives from papers keep their symbol, e.g. $\mathcal{L}_{\text{InfoNCE}}$.
- Time steps of diffusion models and flows are subscripts ($\vect{x}_t$) instead of superscripts ($\vect{x}^{(t)}$).
